cat > /workspace/submission/README.md <<'EOF'
# Certified sharing replay

`python3 submission/main.py` reads one JSON request from stdin to EOF and
writes one JSON response to stdout.  `protocol.py` validates the *whole*
request (including the transactions that follow a restore) before the replay
starts, so an illegal request always answers `{"error":"invalid_request"}`
without partial results.

## Layout

| file | role |
| --- | --- |
| `main.py` | JSON I/O, whole request validation, response serialisation |
| `protocol.py` | request domain, ranges, ids, partitions, walks, tickets, checkpoints |
| `te/session.py` | replay engine: transport registry, generations, checkpoints, events |
| `te/path_providers/base.py` | COO path tensor with stable slots and repaired null slots |
| `te/path_providers/sparse_ops.py` | worker totals, normalised utilisation and mean kernels |
| `te/algorithms/communication/partial_barrier.py` | freshness, acceptance age, progress conditions |
| `te/algorithms/sub_algorithms/admm.py` | consensus vectors, worker bias, scaled dual update |
| `te/algorithms/sub_algorithms/pdlp_mlu.py` | controller projection (analytic, no external solver) |
| `te/algorithms/sub_algorithms/simplex_projection.py` | mass/active-mask simplex and orthant projections |
| `te/algorithms/sub_algorithms/pgd.py` | capacity scaled sharing gradient |
| `te/algorithms/formulations/path_based/distributed/worker.py` | rho scaled worker objective and masked solver |
| `te/algorithms/formulations/path_based/distributed/coordinator.py` | controller step, relaxation and retuning |

## Worker certificate

A worker minimises

    f = 0.5*sum x**2 + 0.5*rho*sum_live (L[e]/c[e] - B[e])**2 - (R if admit)

under `sum_p x[k,p] == d[k]` (route) or `sum_p x[k,p] <= d[k]` (admit) with
`x >= 0`; unavailable slots and zero demand slots are pinned to exactly zero.
The solver computes the KKT point with an exact active set method: every
iteration solves one small dense system, so the reported amounts, raw edge
loads and per commodity potentials (the multipliers `lambda[k]`) satisfy

    G[k,p] + lambda[k] >= 0   (equality for every slot that carries traffic)

and the identity `f = D` of the protocol to machine precision.

## Controller certificate

One advancing step forms `X` from the accepted cache, builds
`V = alpha*X + (1-alpha)*z0 + u0` on the live edges and projects it onto
`{z <= h}` (route, with the ceiling that solves `rho*sum_live (V-h)_+ = 1`) or
onto `{z <= 1}` (admit).  The pressure `t = rho*(V-z)` and the scaled dual
`u = u0 + alpha*X + (1-alpha)*z0 - z` complete the certificate; a retune
rescales `u` so that `rho*u` stays invariant.
EOF
